HCI1.title: Introduction to Human-Computer Interaction
HCI1.content:
What is HCI?

Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) refers to the study and design of the interaction between people and computers, focusing on creating user-friendly interfaces[cite: 3]. It is a multidisciplinary field involving engineering, psychology, design, and ergonomics[cite: 1, 3].

Principles of HCI

Effective interface design is guided by core principles:

  • Know Thy User: Consider factors such as age, gender, education level, social status, and technology background[cite: 3].
  • Understand the Task: Ensure the design matches the steps and logic of the user's workflow[cite: 3].
  • Reduce Memory Load: Minimize the amount of information users must memorize to carry out tasks[cite: 3].
  • Strive for Consistency: Use elements consistently across your application so users are not confused[cite: 3].
  • Remind Users: Employ interfaces that give continuous reminders of important information[cite: 3].
  • Prevent Errors: Eliminate error-prone conditions and provide clear notifications or solutions[cite: 3].
  • Naturalness: Favor natural interaction and interfaces close to human-human communication[cite: 3].

HCI2.title: Guidelines Categories and Example Guidelines
HCI2.content:
Characteristics of HCI Guidelines

HCI guidelines are specific, task-based, user-group focused, and platform-dependent rules[cite: 2, 4].

Types of Guidelines

  • User Type: Tailored for kids, the elderly, or people with disabilities[cite: 2, 4].
  • Platform/System: Designed for mobile, desktop, embedded systems, or public kiosks[cite: 2, 4].
  • Vendor/Brand: Adheres to standards like iOS, Android, Windows, or company branding[cite: 2, 4].
  • Interaction Style: Covers GUI, voice input, gestures, touchscreens, and haptics[cite: 2, 4].

General HCI Design Guidelines

  • Visual Display Layout: Avoid clutter, use alignment and whitespace, and highlight key content[cite: 2, 4].
  • Information Structuring: Organize content logically using navigation aids like breadcrumbs and tabs[cite: 2, 4].
  • Taking User Input: Provide efficient and accurate input methods using drop-downs, checkboxes, and auto-complete[cite: 2, 4].
  • Design for Disabilities: Provide text alternatives for images and allow keyboard-only navigation based on WCAG 2.0[cite: 2, 4].
